fieldValues./summary: Morale checks can govern non-leader NPCs, hirelings, henchmen and intelligent opponents. Casualties, lost leadership and superior enemy force can trigger checks.
fieldValues./bullets/0: Check each round against an obviously superior force. Apply +5% at 25% party casualties, +10% if the leader is unconscious, +15% at 50% or more casualties, and +30% if the leader is slain or deserts; the casualty thresholds also apply to individual wounds.

fieldValues./bullets/3: Failure by 1–15% means fall back fighting; 16–30% disengage and retreat; 31–50% flee in panic; 51% or more surrender.

It explains that each HD above baseline adds an undead die, gives three 6th-level count examples and giant skeleton/zombie scaling, and caps higher-level character remains at ordinary human-skeleton/zombie hit dice. The current card says one per cleric level and does not carry these distinctions.

sourceDenominator.scope: Counts visible example/exception groups; no exhaustive numeric table is present.

siteDisposition.data: Card’s one-per-level baseline remains, but it omits multi-HD creature resolution and the higher-level-character exception.

siteDisposition.search: Captured owner document includes baseline spell but no HD scaling examples/exception; arbitrary query ranking not tested.

sourceAssertions.statement: DMG Cure Blindness does not restore lost visual organs and discusses magical blindness, disease-related conditions (including cataracts, glaucoma and common refractive errors), and other eye disorders. The current card says “most forms” and notes the illusionist Blindness exception, but does not expose these specific limits/examples.

sourceAssertions.statement: DMG Dispel Magic temporarily makes a specially enchanted item non-operational for one round after a successful check, even though its enchantment remains; an item not possessed by a creature receives no saving throw. Current card preserves the no-permanent-removal rule but omits temporary suppression and the no-owner save case.

siteDisposition.data: Card says special-item enchantments are not removed, but has no one-round suppression or possession/save condition.

fieldValues./summary: The outdoor procedure varies both the encounter die and the times of day at which it is checked.

fieldValues./summary: An unguided party can become lost when it lacks a well-defined route or a correct map. The terrain-based check occurs before daily travel.

fieldValues./summary: A flying mount must rest for one hour after every three hours in flight, with no more than nine flight hours in a day.

fieldValues./summary: The general aerial rules make a climb half-speed and a dive double-speed, with maneuverability-class exceptions.
fieldValues./bullets/0: A diving physical attack inflicts double damage against an opponent that is not also diving.
fieldValues./bullets/1: Against a ground target, the qualifying dive begins at least 30 feet above it.
fieldValues./bullets/2: Except class A, a flyer climbs 1 foot for each 3 feet forward and may dive up to 1 foot down per foot forward (45°). Class A may move in any direction.
fieldValues./bullets/3: At full speed the per-round turn and acceleration to full speed are: class A 180° / 1 segment; B 120° / 6 segments; C 90° / 1 round; D 60° / 2 rounds; E 30° / 4 rounds.
fieldValues./bullets/4: Class A stops in 1 segment and class B in 5; both can hover. At half speed creatures turn as one class better; winged creatures except class B cannot remain airborne below half speed.

titleSearch.resultText: Climbing, diving and aerial attacksCombat · DMGRULE

fieldValues./summary: Missile attacks from moving flying mounts, brooms or wings of flying use special range penalties and require substantial practice.
fieldValues./bullets/0: Short range uses the medium-range penalty, −2; medium range uses the long-range penalty, −5; long-range shots miss.
fieldValues./bullets/1: An unpracticed rider using those means cannot hit under this procedure.
fieldValues./bullets/2: A caster hovering with fly or a rider on a hovering flying carpet does not suffer these movement penalties; levitation has separate rules.
fieldValues./bullets/3: A levitating archer attacks at −1, worsening by 1 each successive round of fire to a maximum −3; a round without firing or fighting stabilizes the archer and resets the next shot to −1.
fieldValues./bullets/4: While levitating, slings, thrown javelins or spears, and swung weapons use double those penalties (−2, −4, −6). A medium or heavy crossbow cannot be cocked while levitating.

fieldValues./summary: The aerial damage procedure ties continued flight to how much damage a winged creature has taken.
fieldValues./bullets/0: More than 50% damage prevents maintaining flight and requires landing; more than 75% prevents a controlled descent.
fieldValues./bullets/1: For this flight check, feathered-wing creatures receive an extra allowance equal to half their normal hit points.
fieldValues./bullets/2: That allowance does not add real hit points or prevent death.

fieldValues./summary: For a creature capable of conversation, the DM can roll percentile dice and adjust for charisma and applicable loyalty factors to determine its reaction.

fieldValues./summary: Morale checks can govern non-leader NPCs, hirelings, henchmen and intelligent opponents. Casualties, lost leadership and superior enemy force can trigger checks.
fieldValues./bullets/0: Check each round against an obviously superior force. Apply +5% at 25% party casualties, +10% if the leader is unconscious, +15% at 50% or more casualties, and +30% if the leader is slain or deserts; the casualty thresholds also apply to individual wounds.
fieldValues./bullets/1: Modifiers: each enemy deserting −5%, each enemy slain −10%, inflicting casualties without receiving any −20%, each friend killed +10%, taking casualties without inflicting any +10%, each friend deserting +15%, and being outnumbered and outclassed at least 3 to 1 +20%.
fieldValues./bullets/2: Roll percentile dice against the creature’s morale or loyalty score after adjustments; the amount by which the adjusted roll exceeds the score determines the failure outcome.
fieldValues./bullets/3: Failure by 1–15% means fall back fighting; 16–30% disengage and retreat; 31–50% flee in panic; 51% or more surrender.

siteJoins.relationship: Morale/retreat rules, not personality generation, reaction modifiers or troop-control table.

fieldValues./summary: Morale checks can govern non-leader NPCs, hirelings, henchmen and intelligent opponents. Casualties, lost leadership and superior enemy force can trigger checks.
fieldValues./bullets/0: Check each round against an obviously superior force. Apply +5% at 25% party casualties, +10% if the leader is unconscious, +15% at 50% or more casualties, and +30% if the leader is slain or deserts; the casualty thresholds also apply to individual wounds.
fieldValues./bullets/1: Modifiers: each enemy deserting −5%, each enemy slain −10%, inflicting casualties without receiving any −20%, each friend killed +10%, taking casualties without inflicting any +10%, each friend deserting +15%, and being outnumbered and outclassed at least 3 to 1 +20%.
fieldValues./bullets/2: Roll percentile dice against the creature’s morale or loyalty score after adjustments; the amount by which the adjusted roll exceeds the score determines the failure outcome.
fieldValues./bullets/3: Failure by 1–15% means fall back fighting; 16–30% disengage and retreat; 31–50% flee in panic; 51% or more surrender.

siteJoins.relationship: Base reaction-percentile procedure; not NPC trait-derived modifiers.

fieldValues./summary: For a creature capable of conversation, the DM can roll percentile dice and adjust for charisma and applicable loyalty factors to determine its reaction.
fieldValues./bullets/0: Adjusted percentile 01 or less–05: violently hostile, immediate attack; 06–25: hostile, immediate action. Either can call for a morale check if appropriate.
fieldValues./bullets/1: 26–45: uncertain, 55% prone toward negative; 46–55: neutral, uninterested or uncertain; 56–75: uncertain, 55% prone toward positive.
fieldValues./bullets/2: 76–95: friendly, immediate action; 96–00 or greater: enthusiastically friendly, immediate acceptance.
fieldValues./bullets/3: Circumstances and the creatures involved still matter; a reaction check is not guaranteed cooperation.

sourceAssertions.statement: Printed p.119 defines when to check compatibility, says the DM rolls secretly, supplies nine outcomes (01; 02–03; 04–08; 09–15; 16–25; 26–35; 36–90; 91–99; 00), and includes separate externally mixed outcomes where specified.
sourceAssertions.sourceDenominator: 9 result bands; 1 secret-roll instruction; 1 trigger rule covering 2 conditions; external-mixing effects in the applicable 3 bands.
sourceAssertions.siteDisposition: The owner includes the trigger, secret roll instruction and all nine outcome bands with their damage, cancellation, efficacy and external-mixing qualifiers in visible/searchable fields.

siteJoins.relationship: The secret potion-miscibility procedure and all nine result bands, including external-mixing outcomes and permanent-effect result.

fieldValues./summary: Check the potion-miscibility procedure when potions are physically mixed or when someone drinks another potion while a previous one is still active.
fieldValues./bullets/0: The DM makes the compatibility check secretly.
fieldValues./bullets/1: 01: Explosion; internal damage 6–60 hp and those within 5″ take 1–10 hp. If mixed externally, all within 10 feet take 4–24 hp, no save.
fieldValues./bullets/2: 02–03: Lethal poison kills the imbiber; if mixed externally, a 10-foot-diameter poison cloud requires those within to save versus poison or die.
fieldValues./bullets/3: 04–08: Nausea and −1 strength and dexterity for 5–20 rounds, no save; one potion is cancelled and the other has half strength and duration, determined randomly.
fieldValues./bullets/4: 09–15: Both potions are cancelled. 16–25: One randomly selected potion is cancelled and the other remains normal. 26–35: Both are at half efficacy.
fieldValues./bullets/5: 36–90: Both work normally unless contradictory effects cancel. 91–99: One randomly selected potion has 150% efficacy, subject to the DM deciding whether effect and duration or only duration may increase.
fieldValues./bullets/6: 00: One potion functions permanently on the imbiber; harmful side effects are possible.

sourceAssertions.statement: Printed p.119 says energy drain removes an experience level, its level-gained hit points/abilities, resets XP to the lower-level midpoint, and handles multiclass drains by highest level then class XP requirement. It separately states that a drained 0-level character dies, and that draining all levels can transform the victim into the type of undead that killed them; the source continues with that undead’s control, hit-dice, and advancement/release rules.
sourceAssertions.sourceDenominator: 1 level-loss/XP/HP procedure; 1 multiclass ordering procedure; 1 0-level death outcome; 1 transformation trigger; 1 undead-control/HD and advancement/release procedure.
sourceAssertions.siteDisposition: The owner includes the level loss, midpoint, hit-point and ability loss, and multiclass ordering. It omits the explicit 0-level death outcome and the post-total-drain undead transformation/control/HD/advancement procedure.

siteJoins.relationship: The level/XP/hit-point loss and multiclass ordering portion of the energy-drain rule; its post-zero-level undead outcomes are not included in these fields.

fieldValues./summary: Losing an experience level removes the hit points gained at that level, including its constitution bonus, and the abilities that came with it.
fieldValues./bullets/0: Set experience points to the midpoint of the next lower level.
fieldValues./bullets/1: For multiclass characters, drain the highest class level first; tied levels use the class requiring the most XP.
fieldValues./bullets/2: Recording hit-point gains by level makes later drain and restoration easier to resolve.

fieldValues./bullets/5: 36–90: Both work normally unless contradictory effects cancel. 91–99: One randomly selected potion has 150% efficacy, subject to the DM deciding whether effect and duration or only duration may increase.

currentBefore.summary: Wandering encounters occur through encounter checks; placed encounters arise from the DM's keyed locations. Unnecessary time and noise can attract more danger.
bullets: For an Appendix C dungeon character-party encounter, roll d4 + 1 for 2–5 characters; accompanying men-at-arms or henchmen bring the total party to nine.

In that encounter procedure, men-at-arms accompany parties on dungeon levels 1–3; on level 4 or deeper the companions are henchmen. Character-class incompatibilities and per-party class maxima must also be applied using the source table.

otherRelatedOwners.summary: Henchmen are NPC adventurers supported by a patron. They require upkeep and an appropriate share of treasure, and their loyalty depends on treatment as well as charisma.
Generate abilities using the method your DM permits, then choose race, class and alignment and record languages, money, equipment and hit points.
Plan purchases around both available funds and encumbrance. The campaign may require visiting several sellers, and availability and prices can vary.
Clerics gain daily spells through prayer and meditation. Access to higher spells depends on maintaining the deity's favor rather than finding a wizard-style spellbook.
The ordinary starting method gives read magic automatically and one spell each from the offensive, defensive and miscellaneous selection groups: four spells total.

conditions: Requires line of sight or an unobstructed spell path.
A creature’s successful save places the light immediately behind it instead.
exceptions: Reverse produces darkness for half the light duration.

fields.Material: Holy water circle, or burning incense; reverse uses blood or smoldering dung

effect: Evil attackers suffer −2 to hit; recipient gains +2 on saves against their attacks.
A 1-foot barrier prevents bodily contact by the enchanted, conjured and summoned creatures described in the source.
exceptions: Reverse protects against good while continuing to exclude enchanted evil creatures.

fields.Material: Gem-inlaid sticks, dragon bones or similar tokens; the tea-leaf method also consumes a crushed pearl worth at least 100 gp

effect: Seeks whether an action within the next 3 turns will benefit or harm the party.
conditions: Base accuracy is 70% + 1% per caster level; the referee may adjust for circumstances.

fields.Area: One creature at a time; up to 10 checked

effect: Reveals whether a person or monster is under a charm.
exceptions: The reverse shields only one creature from charm detection.

effect: Makes magically or mechanically concealed traps visible to the cleric.
conditions: The caster must face the direction being inspected.

fields.Saving throw: Special if cast on an unwilling creature

effect: Stops sound throughout the sphere, preventing conversation and spell casting as described in the source.
conditions: May be centered in air, on an object, or on a creature; a creature carries it along.
exceptions: An unwilling creature may save; success centers the effect about 1 foot behind it.

fields.Area: Snakes with total hp no greater than caster’s hp
fields.Maximum affected: One or more snakes whose combined hit points do not exceed the cleric’s hit points.

effect: Makes the snakes cease activity and sway semi-upright.
conditions: Torpid snakes: 1d4+2 turns; calm but active snakes: 1d3 turns; angry or attacking snakes: 1d4+4 rounds.

fields.Area: 1 skeleton or zombie per caster level
fields.Material: A drop of blood, human flesh and bone powder or a bone shard
fields.Maximum affected: One skeleton or zombie per cleric level.

effect: Animates dead human bones or bodies as skeletons or zombies that obey the cleric’s orders.
conditions: Good clerics must weigh the act carefully and have a good reason; the source treats animation as morally problematic.

effect: Permanently cures most forms of blindness.
conditions: Reverse cause blindness requires a successful touch; a successful save negates it.
exceptions: The illusionist Blindness spell explicitly resists cure spells; its caster or dispel magic must remove it (p.95).

effect: Cancels spells on creatures/objects or counters casting in the area. Chance: 50%, +5% per caster level above the original caster, −2% per level below.
Automatically dispels the caster’s own magic.
conditions: Potions can be destroyed and count as 12th level for this check.
exceptions: Does not remove the enchantment from scrolls, rings, wands, weapons, armor and other specially enchanted items.

fields.Casting time: 1 initial segment + 1 segment per square foot protected
fields.Saving throw: Depends on the glyph: negates or halves
fields.Material: Incense; beyond 50 square feet, powdered diamond worth at least 2,000 gp

effect: Sets an invisible ward against unauthorized passage, entry or opening. Touching the protected area without speaking its glyph name triggers it.
conditions: Examples include electrical/fire damage of 2 hp/level, paralysis, blindness or energy drain; the cleric must be high enough to use the chosen glyph.

relevantBeforeFields.summary: A spell's components impose practical casting requirements. Silence or gagging blocks required speech, and restraints can prevent the required gestures.
bullets: Interruption spoils the spell and removes it from memory.
Check the individual spell for its material requirements.

relevantBeforeFields.summary: Casting removes that prepared instance from memory. Multiple copies of the same spell may be prepared within the character's available slots.
bullets: Cross off the cast spell and any expended material components.
Required components must be ready for use.

confirmedRepairCandidates.sourceFact: Printed p.41 has 15 Cleric spell commentary headings (4 first-level, 6 second-level, 5 third-level). Twelve spell entries have bounded partial operational qualifiers, and the general component-use paragraph adds one more partial. Two scoped outcomes are present and four advisory/design/illustrative groups are explicitly excluded. Proposed work is additive, DMG-cited text only; it must not change existing PHB spell values or generalize Cleric-specific notes to other classes.
confirmedRepairCandidates.proposedScope: Add source-labeled, source-limited p.41 qualifiers to the named existing owners, after independent review. Do not propagate these cleric-specific comments to other classes or infer unseen effects.

relatedNonEquivalentOwners.summary: Exploration and map-making slow dungeon travel. Light, probing tools, ropes and a reliable record of the route are practical expedition needs.
Wandering encounters occur through encounter checks; placed encounters arise from the DM's keyed locations. Unnecessary time and noise can attract more danger.
During mapping and exploration, each inch of movement rate gives 10 feet per 10-minute turn. Following a known route is five times as fast.

confirmedRepairCandidates.sourceFact: 24 distinct Appendix A table families contain 198 die-band rows, plus five starter diagrams and the printed solo-play checks; all are pixel-inventoried with explicit row and note denominators. Values are not transcribed here.
confirmedRepairCandidates.proposedScope: If approved, add Appendix A-specific owners or tables with exact source values and notes; preserve dice, dashes, table links, and solo-only limits. Do not treat general dungeon mapping or Appendix C party encounter cards as equivalents.

relatedNonEquivalentOwners.summary: The outdoor procedure varies both the encounter die and the times of day at which it is checked.
An unguided party can become lost when it lacks a well-defined route or a correct map. The terrain-based check occurs before daily travel.
The overland table measures miles per day and reduces travel for both heavier loads and rougher ground.

confirmedRepairCandidates.sourceFact: Appendix B provides a 10×8 d20 terrain matrix (80 slots, five printed dashes), ten guide entries, and a d100 settlement table with nine primary bands and a four-band ruins reroll.
confirmedRepairCandidates.proposedScope: If approved, add Appendix B-specific terrain transition, guide and inhabitation content; retain physical page overlap with Appendix A p.173 and distinguish from existing lost-check, encounter-frequency and overland movement rules.

fields./summary: The PHB offers dwarf, elf, gnome, half-elf, halfling, half-orc and human characters. Racial tables restrict classes and, for many non-human classes, advancement.
fields./bullets/2: PHB class level table (U = unlimited; parenthesized entries are non-player characters only; omitted classes are unavailable to that race): dwarf fighter 9, thief U, assassin 9, cleric (8); elf fighter 7, magic-user 11, thief U, assassin 10, cleric (7); gnome fighter 6, illusionist 7, thief U, assassin 8, cleric (7); half-elf cleric 5, druid U, fighter 8, ranger 8, magic-user 8, thief U, assassin 11; halfling fighter 6, thief U, druid (6); half-orc cleric 4, fighter 10, thief 8, assassin U; human all listed classes U. All are still subject to applicable ability and class requirements.
fields./bullets/3: PHB fighter limits by Strength: dwarf below 17 → 7, at 17 → 8, otherwise maximum 9; elf below 17 → 5, at 17 → 6, otherwise maximum 7; gnome below 18 → 5, otherwise 6; half-elf below 17 → 6, at 17 → 7, otherwise 8. Halfling Hairfeet and others under Strength 17 → 4; Tallfellows at 17 and Stouts at 18 → 5; Tallfellows with 18 → 6.
fields./bullets/4: PHB magic-user limits by Intelligence: elf below 17 → 9, at 17 → 10, otherwise maximum 11; half-elf below 17 → 6, at 17 → 7, otherwise maximum 8. Gnome illusionists with Intelligence or Dexterity below 17 are limited to 5; with both 17 to 6; otherwise table maximum 7. Half-orc thieves with Dexterity below 17 are limited to 6, at 17 to 7, otherwise maximum 8.

fields./summary: A non-human multiclass character divides earned experience equally among the chosen classes, including a class in which the racial level limit has already been reached.
fields./bullets/0: Do not redirect the capped class's share to the other class or classes.

fields./summary: Morale checks can govern non-leader NPCs, hirelings, henchmen and intelligent opponents. Casualties, lost leadership and superior enemy force can trigger checks.
fields./bullets/0: Check each round against an obviously superior force. Apply +5% at 25% party casualties, +10% if the leader is unconscious, +15% at 50% or more casualties, and +30% if the leader is slain or deserts; the casualty thresholds also apply to individual wounds.
fields./bullets/2: Roll percentile dice against the creature’s morale or loyalty score after adjustments; the amount by which the adjusted roll exceeds the score determines the failure outcome.
